replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Math was always a struggle for me, even in school. I never really understood it, and my low education level didn’t help. I stick to basic stuff like counting or measuring for my part-time job, but anything beyond that feels overwhelming. I’d rather spend time on my hobbies, like running or knitting, where I feel more confident and in control.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, honestly, just the thought of math makes me nervous. It brings back bad memories of school where I couldn’t keep up. I avoid it as much as possible. Even simple problems can make my heart race, so I try not to dwell on it. It’s not something I enjoy or see the need for in my daily life.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: No, I’ve never tried using AI for math. I don’t even know where to start with that. The idea of using technology to help with something I already struggle with feels pointless. I’d rather ask someone I trust, like a coworker, for help with basic tasks. It’s simpler and less intimidating for me.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: I’m not sure I can explain that—I barely understand it myself. But from what I remember vaguely, you’d move terms around to get everything on one side, then maybe use something called ‘factoring’ or ‘quadratic formula.’ But honestly, it’s all a blur. I’d need to look it up or ask someone else to help me figure it out.

I’ve never heard of ‘stationary points’ before, so I can’t explain that. It sounds complicated and way beyond what I’ve ever learned. I’d probably just skip over it or ask someone who knows math better. It’s not something I’d worry about in my daily life, so I don’t see the point in trying to understand it.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis? That sounds like advanced stuff I’ve never even heard of. If you’re asking me to explain it, I’d say it’s way too complex for me. I’d get anxious just thinking about it. Stick to simpler math, or just avoid it altogether—it’s not something I can handle or see the use for.
replies.According to you, how can LLMs be used t: I don’t really see how those AI things would help me, but maybe for kids or students who struggle less than I did? Perhaps they could explain math in simpler words or give step-by-step examples. But honestly, I’d rather have a real teacher or someone who can show me math in a way that makes sense. Technology might not work for everyone, especially those who find math as scary as I do.
